page.layout: One column of running text, with a woodcut initial at the start of the first paragraph. Page number at top left, running head at top centre. Head "CONCIO LVIII" with "Tit. 2." below it, both centred. No margin notes or footnotes.

spitis, qui præsens est, & nos alit perpetuò,

nobis adsit sua gratia, suoque spiritu, ut pos-
simus omnia, sive edamus, sive bibamus, si-

Jesum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
CONCIO LVIII
Tit. 2.
Tu vero loquere quæ decent sa-
nam doctrinam. Senes ut so-
brii sint, graves, modesti, sa-
næ fide, charitate, patientia.
Anus itidem, ut in habitu sint qui reli-
gionem deceat, non calumniatrices, vino
multo servientes, ut honesta doceant, quæ
possint modestas reddere adolescentulas,
ut maritos suos diligant, ut liberos a-
ment, ut sobriæ sint, pura, domus custo-
des, bonæ, subditæ suis viris, ne sermo Dei
male audiat. Adolescentes similiter
adhortare, ut sobrii sint, per omnia te-
metipsum præbens formam bonorum o-
perum in doctrina, integritatem, gravit-
atem, sermonem sanum, irreprehensibi-lem:

page.notes: Page number printed as "44º" with a raised o; read as 440 in the running text. The woodcut initial is decorative and reads as T, joined to "u" of "Tu". Small ornamental marks stand before "Anus" and "Adolescentes" and after "adhortare"; they are not letters and were left out, except that the mark after "adhortare" may be a printed abbreviation sign, which I have not reproduced. The paragraph is kept as one unbroken paragraph, since the lines run to the margin without indents.
